questions.question: According to the testing pyramid, what shape should a healthy test suite generally have?
options: Mostly end-to-end tests, with a few unit tests
Many fast unit tests, fewer integration tests, and only a handful of end-to-end tests covering critical flows
Exactly equal numbers of each type of test
Only end-to-end tests are necessary; unit tests are redundant
questions.explanation: Unit tests are fast and cheap so you write many; E2E tests are slow and brittle so you reserve them for your most critical flows, with integration tests in between.

questions.question: Why is a pure function like `sum(a, b)` especially easy to unit test?
options: Pure functions cannot be tested at all
It requires no setup or mocking — just call it with inputs and assert the output, since it has no external dependencies or side effects
You need a real database to test it properly
questions.explanation: Because a pure function's output depends only on its inputs, with no side effects or dependencies, testing it is as simple as asserting on the returned value.

questions.question: Why mock `fetch` when testing `getTemperature(city)` instead of letting it make a real network request?
options: Mocking is required by every testing framework and has no real benefit
It makes the test fast, deterministic, and isolated from network conditions or the real external API's current behavior
fetch cannot be called inside a test environment under any circumstances
It makes the test slower but more "realistic"
questions.explanation: Mocking removes the real network dependency, so the test runs instantly and reliably, specifically verifying getTemperature's own logic rather than the real API's availability.

questions.question: What is the main distinction between an integration test and a unit test?
options: Integration tests only run in CI, never locally
A unit test isolates one function/module with dependencies mocked out; an integration test exercises several units working together, closer to real behavior but slower to run
There is no real difference between them
Unit tests can only test asynchronous code
questions.explanation: Unit tests isolate a single piece with mocks; integration tests verify that multiple real pieces correctly work together, trading some speed for more realistic coverage.
